cues.zh: -[旁白] 过去半个世纪最令人兴奋的科学发现之一
cues.en: -[narrator] One of the most exciting scientific findings of the past half-century

cues.zh: 就是广泛存在的营养级联现象的发现。
cues.en: has been the discovery of widespread trophic cascades.

cues.zh: 营养级联是一种生态过程，它始于食物链的顶端
cues.en: A trophic cascade is an ecological process which starts at the top of the food chain

cues.zh: 并一路向下层层传递。
cues.en: and tumbles all the way down to the bottom.

cues.zh: 最经典的例子发生在美国黄石国家公园
cues.en: And the classic example is what happened in the Yellowstone National Park

cues.zh: 那是1995年狼群被重新引入的时候。
cues.en: in the United States when wolves were reintroduced in 1995.

cues.zh: 我们都知道狼会捕杀各种动物，
cues.en: Now, we all know that wolves kill various species of animals,

cues.zh: 但也许我们不太了解的是，它们也赋予了许多其他生命。
cues.en: but perhaps we're slightly less aware that they give life to many others.

cues.zh: 在狼群出现之前——它们已经消失了70年——
cues.en: Before the wolves turned up-- they'd been absent for 70 years--

cues.zh: 鹿的数量，因为没有什么来捕猎它们，
cues.en: the numbers of deer, because there was nothing to hunt them,

cues.zh: 在黄石公园里不断增长、不断增长，
cues.en: had built up and built up in the Yellowstone Park,

cues.zh: 尽管人类努力控制它们，
cues.en: and despite efforts by humans to control them,

cues.zh: 它们还是把那里的大部分植被啃得几乎精光。
cues.en: they'd managed to reduce much of the vegetation there to almost nothing.

cues.zh: 它们刚刚把这片区域啃食殆尽。
cues.en: They had just grazed it away.

cues.zh: 但狼群一到，尽管数量很少，
cues.en: But as soon as the wolves arrived, even though they were few in number,

cues.zh: 却开始产生极其显著的影响。
cues.en: they started to have the most remarkable effects.

cues.zh: 首先，它们当然杀死了一些鹿，但那并不是主要的影响。
cues.en: First, of course, they killed some of the deer, but that wasn't the major thing.

cues.zh: 更重要的是，它们彻底改变了鹿的行为。
cues.en: Much more significantly, they radically changed the behavior of the deer.

cues.zh: 鹿开始避开公园里的某些区域——
cues.en: The deer started avoiding certain parts of the park--

cues.zh: 那些它们最容易被困住的地方——
cues.en: the places where they could be trapped most easily--

cues.zh: 尤其是山谷和峡谷，
cues.en: particularly the valleys and the gorges,

cues.zh: 而那些地方立刻开始重新生长。
cues.en: and immediately those places started to regenerate.

cues.zh: 在某些区域，树木的高度仅仅六年就增长到了原来的五倍。
cues.en: In some areas, the height of the trees quintupled in just six years.

cues.zh: 光秃的山谷两侧很快变成了白杨、柳树和三角叶杨的森林。
cues.en: Bare valley sides quickly became forests of aspen and willow and cottonwood.

cues.zh: 而这一切一发生，鸟类就开始迁入。
cues.en: And as soon as that happened, the birds started moving in.

cues.zh: 鸣禽和候鸟的数量开始大幅增加。
cues.en: The number of songbirds and migratory birds started to increase greatly.

cues.zh: 海狸的数量开始增加，因为海狸喜欢吃树。
cues.en: The number of beavers started to increase because beavers like to eat the trees.

cues.zh: 而海狸和狼一样，都是生态系统工程师。
cues.en: And beavers, like wolves, are ecosystem engineers.

cues.zh: 它们为其他物种创造了生态位。
cues.en: They create niches for other species.

cues.zh: 它们在河里筑起的水坝
cues.en: And the dams they built in the rivers

cues.zh: 为水獭、麝鼠、鸭子
cues.en: provided habitats for otters and muskrats and ducks

cues.zh: 以及鱼类、爬行动物和两栖动物提供了栖息地。
cues.en: and fish and reptiles and amphibians.

cues.zh: 狼捕杀了郊狼，因此
cues.en: The wolves killed coyotes, and as a result of that,

cues.zh: 兔子和老鼠的数量开始上升，
cues.en: the number rabbits and mice began to rise,

cues.zh: 这意味着更多的鹰、
cues.en: which meant more hawks,

cues.zh: 更多的黄鼠狼、
cues.en: more weasels,

cues.zh: 更多的狐狸、
cues.en: more foxes,

cues.zh: 更多的獾。
cues.en: more badgers.

cues.zh: 渡鸦和白头海雕飞下来，以狼留下的腐肉为食。
cues.en: Ravens and bald eagles came down to feed on the carrion that the wolves had left.

cues.zh: 熊也以此为食，它们的数量同样开始上升，
cues.en: Bears fed on it, too, and their population began to rise as well,

cues.zh: 部分原因还在于再生的灌木上长出了更多浆果。
cues.en: partly also because there were more berries growing on the regenerating shrubs.

cues.zh: 而熊又强化了狼的影响
cues.en: And the bears reinforced the impact of the wolves

cues.zh: 它们杀死了一些小鹿。
cues.en: by killing some of the calves of the deer.

cues.zh: 但真正有趣的地方在这里。
cues.en: But here's where it gets really interesting.

cues.zh: 狼改变了河流的行为。
cues.en: The wolves changed the behavior of the rivers.

cues.zh: 河流的蜿蜒减少了，
cues.en: They began to meander less,

cues.zh: 侵蚀减少了，
cues.en: there was less erosion,

cues.zh: 河道变窄了，
cues.en: the channels narrowed,

cues.zh: 形成了更多水潭、更多浅滩段——
cues.en: more pools formed, more riffle sections--

cues.zh: 这些对野生动物栖息地都非常有利。
cues.en: all of which were great for wildlife habitats.

cues.zh: 河流因狼而改变。
cues.en: The rivers changed in response to the wolves.

cues.zh: 原因是再生的森林
cues.en: And the reason was that the regenerating forests

cues.zh: 稳固了河岸，使河岸坍塌得更少，
cues.en: stabilized the banks so that they collapsed less often,

cues.zh: 于是河流的走向变得更加固定。
cues.en: so that the rivers became more fixed in their course.

cues.zh: 同样，通过把鹿赶出某些地方，
cues.en: Similarly, by driving the deer out of some places,

cues.zh: 以及山谷两侧植被的恢复，
cues.en: and the vegetation recovering on the valley sides,

cues.zh: 土壤侵蚀减少了，因为植被也稳固了土壤。
cues.en: there was less soil erosion because the vegetation stabilized that as well.

cues.zh: 于是，数量并不多的狼群，
cues.en: So the wolves, small in number,

cues.zh: 不仅改变了黄石国家公园的生态系统，
cues.en: transformed not just the ecosystem of the Yellowstone National Park,

cues.zh: 这片辽阔的土地，甚至还改变了它的自然地貌。
cues.en: this huge area of land, but also its physical geography.
